chapter_theme: The lament turns inward to the dismantling of the self: before the body is thrown away, to learn the impossible art of milking the stone cow; to be as one dead, without breath, speech, memory or forgetting; to lose my will, the world's hold and even self-command and rest on grace; to forget myself, the place, karma and even the Lord and be alone; to bar the head-door and sleep within. Similes of pervasion (oil in sesame, juice in cane, the swan parting milk from water, the lotus in the sky) frame the void and the supreme space in which maya is to die, and the chapter ends in bliss that staggers like toddy, and in the eye of wisdom that sees all as him and still takes refuge.
structure_note: No fixed order; the couplets alternate similes (206 to 208, 212, 213, 218, 221) with direct askings. 214 to 217 form a run on losing will and forgetting; 222 is a unit from the second edition, placed between 221 and 223. Every couplet ends on the refrain எக்காலம்.

201.reading: Before this evil body is thrown away, when will I learn to milk the stone cow's milk?
201.nuance: Milk from a stone cow is a stock figure of the impossible, yet here it is a skill (கற்பது) to be learned in this life. Tradition reads it as drawing the yogic nectar from the hard body or from the skull; plainly it is doing the impossible before death. பொல்லாத காயம் is the poet's standing contempt for the body.

202.reading: Sadasiva who shines within the bare open space: when will I seek him so that he comes near and shows me kindness?
202.nuance: சதாசிவம் is the Siddhanta name for the Lord at the level where he is reached by souls; he is placed in the வெட்டவெளி of 187 and 188. கிருபை செய்வது has the Lord as its agent.

203.reading: Setting my mind unmoving in the great awareness, when will I stand rooted every day in the one awareness?
203.nuance: பேரறிவு and ஓரறிவு, the great awareness and the one awareness, are the same thing named from two sides: its size and its singleness.

204.reading: The way that stood within my soul, as if non-dual, to give release: when will I know it?
204.nuance: அத்துவிதம் போலும் is hedged: போலும் is 'like', so the way is only advaita-like, or an assertive particle, so it is advaita indeed. The poet names the doctrine without quite claiming it.

205.reading: Not perishing while I remain in the bond I stand in, when will I spread into the form in which you stand?
205.nuance: The bond (பாசம்) is the poet's present place, and the Lord's form (கோலம்) the place to be reached; the fear is of dying still in the bond.

206.reading: As with sesame, sugarcane, the fine flower and the body, standing inside and outside, when will I reach and know it?
206.nuance: Four containers of something hidden in them: oil, juice, scent, and the self in the body. The Lord is said to stand both within these and outside them; 159 used the sesame alone.

207.reading: As the swan parts the water off and drinks the nectar, when will I part myself off and sweetly see you?
207.nuance: The swan that separates milk from water is the stock figure of discrimination. என்னை வகுத்து, dividing myself, is the seeker's own sorting of what in him is water and what is nectar.

208.reading: Like a lotus that flowered on water in the sky and rose open, when will I hold my mind steady and have sight of you?
208.nuance: அந்தரத்தில் நீர்பூத்து, water flowering in space, is a strange image for an ordinary lotus; tradition takes the lotus in the inner sky as the lotus at the crown, opened by meditation. Plainly it is any lotus rising clear of the water.

209.reading: Without birth and death, without speech and breath, without forgetting and remembering, when will I be as one dead?
209.nuance: மாண்டிருப்பது, to be dead, is asked for as a state while alive: the three pairs removed are the marks of ordinary life. The stopped breath (மூச்சும் அற்று) is the yogic sign of the state.

210.reading: Shutting the enduring supreme space inside the space of the mind, when will I raise awareness within me as one thought?
210.nuance: The large is enclosed in the small: the supreme space (பரவெளி) is held within the mind-space (மனவெளி), and from it a single thought is to rise. This single thought is the exception to the thoughtlessness asked elsewhere (166, 219).

211.reading: Putting away the dream of desire I have for women, when will I take up the sound of you and subside?
211.nuance: Desire for women is a dream (கனவு) to be ended; what replaces it is sound (ஓசை), the Lord heard rather than seen, as in 191 and 197.

212.reading: As I wandered carrying my own life, when will I carry your life and subside here?
212.nuance: To live by the Lord's life instead of one's own: the exchange is of the animating principle, not of conduct. இங்கு, here, keeps the goal in this world.

213.reading: This firm body, like a branch planted in mud: when will I see it as a puppet whirling in the wind?
213.nuance: சூத்திரம் is the string, hence the puppet worked by it; காற்று is the wind and also the breath, so the body is a puppet worked by the breath on a yogic reading. The planted branch looks rooted but is cut wood.

214.reading: My will lost, the hold that was here lost, and self-command lost, when will I rest upon grace?
214.nuance: Three வசம்: என் வசம் (my control), இங்கிருந்த வசம் (the hold that was here, the world's or the body's), தன்வசம் (one's own self-possession). The third is the hardest to place; it may mean the self's command of itself, so that even surrender is not to be one's own act.

215.reading: Forgetting myself, forgetting the state of the place, forgetting karma, when will I gain the goal?
215.nuance: தலத்து நிலை is the state of the place, the world one stands in, or in cipher the bodily centres (தலம்). கதி is the good end, release.

216.reading: Forgetting me within myself, forgetting even the Lord who was there, forgetting myself by myself, when will I be alone?
216.nuance: Even the Lord (பதி) is to be forgotten, which puts the state past worship and past 161's plea that he never leave. தனித்து இருப்பது is the solitary state, the kaivalya of yoga.

217.reading: Forgetting myself by myself, barring the head-door, when will I sleep within, thinking of you?
217.nuance: தலைவாசல் is plainly the front door, which one bolts before sleep; in cipher it is the door at the head, the crown or the gates of the senses, barred so that the breath and mind do not go out. The sleep is the inward rest of 158, not slumber.

218.reading: Like the anril bird, which has its joy only in not being parted from its mate, when my companion is parted from me, when will I take hold of the thread of grace and follow it?
218.nuance: The anril is the bird of lore that dies when parted from its mate, so இன்பமுறும் (finds joy) in the first line is surprising and the text may be faulty. துணை, the companion, may be the body, a human partner or the guru. தூல் is read as நூல், thread.

219.reading: With no dance at all and not the least movement to be seen, when will I seek the sky-thing that has no seeking?
219.nuance: தேட்டம் is both searching and the thing sought or desired; the verse asks to seek, in stillness, what is beyond seeking and desire, and keeps the paradox.

220.reading: If by former deeds my knowledge fails to ripen and then hides away, when will I seek the Mother and drink nectar?
220.nuance: The syntax is loose: the conditional about unripe knowledge seems to be the obstacle, and the Mother's nectar the cure. அன்னை is Shakti, and the nectar is the yogic amrita or simply the mother's milk the child seeks.

221.reading: By the bliss that gives delight as toddy does to the drinker, when will I be pushed about, stand dancing and be brought to a halt?
221.nuance: Drunkenness is used without disapproval as the figure for bliss; தடைப்படுவது, being stopped, is the end of the stagger, when the drunk can go no further.

222.reading: The egoism that says 'I' and the tattvas destroyed and gone, when will the very speech of 'I' come to rest?
222.nuance: A unit from the second edition. ஆணவம் is the primal mala of Siddhanta, here named with its characteristic word 'I'. தங்கிநிற்பது can mean to stay or to be stilled; the sense wants the 'I'-talk to cease, but the verb can be read the other way.

223.reading: Knowing with the eye of wisdom that all I see is 'I am he', standing as he, when will I take refuge?
223.nuance: நான் அவனாய் is the 'I am he' of Vedanta, yet the line ends in சரண் அடைதல், taking refuge, which needs two. The poet holds identity and surrender in one breath.

224.reading: Within the endless Supreme, seeing bliss, when will I sit settled?

225.reading: Gazing intently into the space that has come near, there in the sky, when will maya die out and leave nothing?
225.nuance: The gazing (உற்றுப் பார்த்து) is the practice and maya's death the result; மற்றமற, without remainder, insists nothing of it is left.

links.note: The swan that parts milk from water in both. In Tirumular the parter is the Lord or guru, who turns the soul's deeds into roasted seeds; in Pattiragiriyar it is the seeker, who must part himself from himself to see the Lord.

Both make being dead while alive the mark of the knower: Tirumular's Siva-gnanis go about dead with senses and body intact; Pattiragiriyar asks to be dead without birth, death, speech, breath, memory or forgetting. Pattiragiriyar adds the stopped breath, which makes his state yogic as well as moral.
166 asks that nothing attach in thought; 210 asks to raise one thought within, awareness itself, with the supreme space shut in the mind. The one thought is the exception to the emptiness of 166.
Two ways of saying that the self must not run on its own: 212 exchanges one's own life for the Lord's, 214 loses my will, the world's hold and self-command and rests on grace.

The puppet moved from outside in both: Tirumular's deed makes a false puppet dance as the Lord makes the elements dance; Pattiragiriyar's body is a puppet whirled by the wind. Tirumular names the mover (deed, then grace); Pattiragiriyar asks only to see the body as puppet.

Both shut a door and turn in: Tirumular locks the breath as with a bolt and turns the gaze back to rest within the eye; Pattiragiriyar bars the head-door and sleeps within thinking of the Lord. The link depends on reading தலைவாசல் as a door in the body, which is one of two readings.

The anril that never parts from its mate is the figure of fidelity in both: in the Naladiyar it is the courtesan's broken promise never to part; in Pattiragiriyar it is the soul that should cling to grace when its companion is parted. The bird is the same, the bond is a lover's in one and the Lord's in the other.

Both set bliss beside toddy: Tirumular contrasts the yogi's nectar of knowledge-bliss with the fool's liquor, Pattiragiriyar uses the drunkard's staggering as the picture of bliss itself. The image is shared, with opposite valuation of the drunk.

source_issues: Unit 222 (id siddhar:meynjanap-pulambal:0155-192) is from a second edition: unnumbered in the main edition, without the refrain's question mark, interleaved between 221 and 223.
218 first line: இன்பமுறும் gives the anril joy on parting, against the lore that it dies on parting; the text looks faulty. தூல் in the second line is read as நூல்.
223 prints ஞானவிழியா ல்அறிந்து with a space inside the word.
